comment: Expected behaviour of every case that runs in minutes.  A change that
moves any of these numbers is a change in the answer and has to be
justified by a measurement, not by the fact that the next wall passed.
Numbers were recorded at commit 2e3bef3 on 1 thread; they are trajectory
quantities, so an A/B must fix OMP_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS on
both arms (runs are NOT reproducible across thread counts).
required_lines: every run's log must contain these, so a report that silently stopped being emitted is caught.

cases.name: fast-plain
cases.what: the bar with a partial cohesive plane: bulk damage, deletion, cutbacks

cases.name: fast-plain-smooth
cases.what: the regulariser on a deck with real bulk damage and 90 deletions where no DAMAGED facet ever closes: it must be a byte-for-byte no-op, because the blend differs from the sharp law only when g<1 AND the facet is in compression

cases.name: fast-wrapped
cases.what: the eroding phase wrapped in facets: reaches a node with no bulk support, and walls on the crack-face kink

cases.name: fast-wrapped-smooth
cases.what: the same deck with the crack-face kink regularised: the wall is gone and the fracture is not

cases.name: fast-wrapped-nospc
cases.what: the same wall without the load-path mask, which must not change it

cases.name: mixed-analytic
cases.what: inclined cohesive plane against the closed-form post-peak branch, 36 percent shear

cases.name: mixed-analytic-smooth
cases.what: the same, with the kink regulariser armed: that facet never closes, so it must be bit-identical

cases.name: close-sharp
cases.what: the UC6 normal law itself, verified point by point on a facet damaged to gmin and then closed: this is where the five-orders tangent jump is measured rather than argued

cases.name: close-blend
cases.what: the same facet under the regulariser: identical far-field slopes, so nothing physical moved, and the blend band actually exercised
